confidence_rationale: The five sources are all secondary observers rather than Djiboutian state disclosures, and two of the five (allafrica.com, aljazeera.com) sit at tier 3. Two of the low scores rest on the absence of published state data rather than on a positive finding, and the Amnesty International country page could not be retrieved (HTTP 504). The direction of the movement is well supported; the exact magnitude is not independently corroborated.
rationale: Djibouti is published at composite 20.3 on a never-assessed uniform seed vector (2/2/2/1.5/2/1.5/2/1.5) shared byte-identically by twelve countries at ranks 134-145 of the countries index. A full 40-subdimension assessment dated 2026-08-16 replaces that seed with evidence and returns 17.5, a delta of -2.8 points. That delta is below the 5.0-point filing threshold but the band changes from Developing to Critical, so the proposal is filed under the band-crossing clause.

notes: Filed under the revised band-crossing clause: a proposal may be filed when EITHER the absolute composite delta is at least 5.0 points OR the assessed band differs from the published band, at any delta. This proposal is filed on the second condition. The composite delta is -2.8 points, which would NOT have been filable under the previous 5.0-point-only rule, and the original Djibouti assessment therefore recorded "do not file" on that basis. The movement is a seed-baseline de-seeding, not a finding of new misconduct: Djibouti was published on a never-assessed uniform seed vector (2/2/2/1.5/2/1.5/2/1.5, composite 20.3) shared byte-identically by twelve countries at ranks 134-145 of the countries index. Replacing that placeholder with 40 measured subdimension scores moves the composite to 17.5, which crosses the 20.0 boundary from Developing into Critical. No subdimension score, evidence item or composite has been re-scored or altered for this filing; every value is carried verbatim from the 2026-08-16 assessment and its sidecar.
